title: Research note: restoration coalescing across a recursion batch (read-free + composable-family boundary; no new kappa)
body:
## Status: research note (scoped mechanism + complete cost recurrence; no new kappa)

Track **recursive-interfaces** (50-59), assignment seed **53** (OS CSPRNG). One
explicit way to eliminate boundary/restoration work with a complete cost
recurrence, a sufficient correctness condition (with the exact defect criterion
behind it), and a sharp cost boundary. Contributor:
**Navinor (Aaron Wang)**, with help from opencode. Apache-2.0.

### What is learned

A recursion node that restores its borrowed dirty workspace after **every** child
pays `r` restoration passes. This note prices one operator-level rewrite: let the
workspace drift across the batch and replace the `r` restorations by the **one**
composed restoration `(G_r...G_1)^{-1}` at the node exit. Two independent
questions decide it, both decidable exactly:

- **Correctness (vanishing defect; read-free is sufficient, not necessary).**
  The single deferred restoration returns the same observables (final data and
  final workspace) exactly when the summed defect vanishes,
  `sum_i B_i (G_{i-1}...G_1 - I) = 0`. Read-free batches make every term vanish
  separately and are sufficient, but they are **not necessary**: nonzero readers
  can cancel (exact counterexamples:
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1199,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1203,
  https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1205). The certificate's
  reader example shows only that one reader child *can* break deferral; a second
  case replays the exact nonzero-reader cancellation (5 restorations -> 1).
- **Cost (composable family; density is not application cost).** The rewrite
  removes passes only when the restoration operators stay cheap under
  composition: unit phases -> one phase pass, permutations -> one routing pass
  (`r -> 1`). A **heterogeneous** mix (phase + Walsh + permutation) composes to
  a dense product that *retains its cheap factorization*: applying the factors
  sequentially costs the eager sum (`16` = `16` multiplications at `N = 8`,
  verified against the exact dense product). Deferred application costs *more*
  only when no cheap factorization is retained and the dense product must be
  applied directly (`64` vs `16` multiplications at `N = 8` — a statement about
  direct dense application). Structure, not the count alone, decides.

### Reproduce

Standard library only, Python 3.10+ (verified on 3.12 and 3.13), from the repo root:

```sh
python3 -I -O -B research/restoration-coalescing/verify.py
```

Expected first line:

```
PASS_RESTORATION_COALESCING phase=3->1(x3) perm=3->1 hetero_dense=True reader_diverges=True reader_cancels_5to1=True hetero_mults=eager16|factorized16|dense64
```

The checker recomputes the certificate and compares every field with
`research/restoration-coalescing/CERTIFICATE.json`, failing on drift. It builds
every operator explicitly at `N = 8` over exact Gaussian rationals (no floating
point, no random tolerance, no imported supplier verifier), derives each composed
restoration from the exact dense product, and self-checks any cheap structured
application against that product on the standard basis before trusting its cost.

### Base commit and pins

- Base: `ce7ad1b6ab09452c3478723a2e96ed5ff212dc08` (current `origin/main`).
- Branch: `research/agent-13-recursive-seed53` (isolated research
  package under `research/restoration-coalescing/`; no generator, `upstream/`, or
  selected-construction file touched).
- Selected result at base unchanged: `kappa = 836330098538459/500000000000000000`
  (CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1094 on CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1087).
- Exact source/dependency pins and file digests: `research/restoration-coalescing/SOURCE-PINS.json`.

### Relationship to concurrent work

This is a second, independent treatment of the restoration question with a
meaningfully different method (exact operator algebra and structure detection,
standalone sub-second, versus assembly-level pricing on frozen payloads). It does
**not** claim priority on "restoration deferral" and does not reproduce others'
numbers.

- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1012)
  (thakrarsagar, same track) prices restoration deferral of U8 helper rank/frame
  climbs at the hosted T37 assembly level and finds it mass-neutral. Different
  layer and cost unit (rank mass vs. phase/routing passes); complementary, not a
  contradiction.
- [CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#974](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/974)
  (avirazza, same track) prices the same boundary classes with zero parent cost.

Where those notes give the assembly-level ceiling effect, this note gives the
operator-level preconditions (vanishing summed defect + composable family) for a
genuine
`r -> 1` pass reduction at all. Both are needed before deferral is placed in a
real supplier call.

### Scope and inherited assumptions

A restoration-elimination mechanism, its recurrence, and its exact applicability
boundary. **Not** a construction, not a new kappa, not an all-size physical
compiler, precision contract, common tape, analytic transfer, owner schedule, or
the integer-multiplication theorem. Finite checks are exact algebraic identities
and exact cost counts; they do not certify a whole E8 word or the selected
`kappa`. Neither the selected frontier nor `upstream/` changes. Inherited
all-size/compiler, hosting, precision/tape and analytic assumptions remain with
their existing constructions. No independent human or proof-assistant review is
claimed. Relevant check run: the package's own verifier (full `make verify` and
the selected cold replay are untouched by this isolated package and were not run).
